description: A query operator stores what to do and runs only when its result is enumerated, so it sees the source as it is at that moment.
Operators that return a single value or a materialized collection, such as `Count`, `First` and `ToList`, run the query as soon as they are called.
Streaming operators such as `Where` yield elements as they read them, while non-streaming ones such as `OrderBy` and `GroupBy` must read the whole source first.
Enumerating the same deferred sequence more than once, which repeats its work and side effects each time and is flagged by analyzer rule CA1851.
Running a query once and storing its results with `ToList`, `ToArray`, `ToDictionary` or an async equivalent.
A data structure describing a lambda, which the compiler builds for `IQueryable<T>` queries so a provider can translate them, for example into SQL.
A sequence backed by a query provider such as EF Core, whose operators compose a translated query instead of running delegates in memory.
EF Core running part of a query in the application: allowed in the final `Select`, and an exception anywhere else since EF Core 3.0 unless you switch explicitly with `AsEnumerable`.
